how: Rows 1-5 are host mutations: one edit applied to the working tree with python3 /tmp/x34-mut2.py, the named suite run against it (`bun run test -- --runTestsByPath …`), and the file restored before the next row; `before` is the shipped source the row was run against, `after` the text that replaced it. Rows 6-8 are red proofs against the branch's own shipped state rather than synthetic edits: the drift or the missing function is the mutation, so each row names the commit it was red under. Rows 9-13 are the host Swift ones for the same wait, run through `test:native`. The last three rows are the device proofs on lease X34-vv27s: each mutated the UITests source, rebuilt, and ran a filtered gate whose name satisfies nothing but itself, with the file restored and rebuilt before the ledger's final line. Lease X34-vv27s, pair-b (nitro-ui B / iOS 27.0 and emulator-5570 / API 35, Metro 8293). Logs: `node scripts/gate.mjs logs --branch task/X34-gate-hygiene`.

mutations.run: bun run test -- --runTestsByPath scripts/__tests__/gate-runner.test.js -t "sends the real term" — FAIL, 1 of 1 run (15.4 s)
redTests: sends the real term to the GROUP: - Expected - 1 / + Received + 6 at scripts/__tests__/gate-runner.test.js:454 — the escalation spy recorded the by-pid SIGKILLs the term was supposed to make unnecessary, and the sweep returned the survivor
mutations.note: This row is a coverage gap, not a fixed bug: the same mutation passed all 35 tests that existed when it was first run (17:05), because every other `stopGroup` case injects `signal`. The sign in `process.kill(-group, …)` is the difference between taking a run's tree down and orphaning its Metro, which is exactly X32's incident, and nothing in the suite could see it. The new case is the real call on a real group.
